text_fidelity_a:
Mirrycle MTB Bar End Mountain Bicycle Mirror , Black Just installed the Mirrycle bicycle mirror today and took it for a test run.

A few observations and comments.

Agreed, assembly is not entirely easy. As mentioned by numerous reviews, the screws drive hard to the point that you think you’re actually cracking the plastic plus the included Allen wrench requires some strength to turn. But not to worry. Read the instructions and they’ll confirm the hard drive and that you will not crack the plastic. I didn’t try WD40 or any other lubricant so cannot say if that would ease the assembly.

I installed the Mirrycle onto a GT hybrid bicycle and after using a Dremel tool to create an opening in the end of my handle grip I found the handlebar opening accepted the smaller of the two wedges for mounting. I chose to follow the alternative down and under installation mentioned on Amazon reviews which is quite clever and works very well however I believe you may get a better site picture using the “normal” above and to the side installation which would facilitate not having to move your eyes so far from your frontal path to do so. The primary disadvantage to the “normal” up-and-out installation is that the mirror really sticks out there very exposed and if/when you dump your bike or ride close to any shrubs, etc., your mirror will be the early casualty, plus the storage shed where we keep our bikes is small which would necessitate tucking the mirror in upon each return. Do whichever works best for you.

From the lower mounting position I could see both myself and directly behind me but I don’t believe that provides the maximum field of view. On my initial trip I stopped a couple times to adjust the mirror in a similar manner to what you would do with a car, i.e., if you can see part of yourself/your bike in the mirror, tilt it out just a little further until you can’t and that should be about right. Once adjusted properly you only need to tilt your head a tad one way to see either part of yourself directly behind the mirror or a tad the other way to see much more of the road to your direct left.

I was amazed at how solid this mirror rode exhibiting absolutely no jitter or vibration. The large convex shape offered a wide, clear field of view which allowed me not only to see what was coming from behind me but also what was to the near left rear of me as well.

This was only my first day with this product but I’m impressed with the quality and the flexible mounting options it offers.
text_fidelity_b: Mirrycle MTB Bar End Mountain Bicycle Mirror , Black

text_fidelity_a:
The Omega Project Black Book Training Journal – US Army Special Operations Elite Workout Planner – Leather Fitness Tracker Notebook Logs Exercise, Sleep, Recovery, Nutrition and More I like this nutrition journal because it addresses unhealthy attitudes about food. Because it is based in a cognitive behavioral therapy approach, it really comes down to values. Do I value my life more than I value instant gratification? Am I living my values? This method doesn't preach nor are the expectations too vigorous as I can modify the exercise to take into account my disability and nutritional requirements. It approaches nutrition, body composition, and the mental attitudes that lead to unhealthy eating as simply as can be. But at no time is it turning a deaf ear to how difficult it can be to actually make changes. That's why the journalling is so important. Further, you can customize for yourself your physical ability or dietary needs. It isn't really about if you can run a mile in 5 minutes, but about whether you take a step towards your goal.

As adults, we are all responsible for our choices and for what we do with our lives. Maybe it isn't my fault that I have an unhealthy attitude towards food, but it is each of our responsibility to love ourselves enough to be willing to change. This journal is not going to magically fix 30 years of unhealthy thinking or eating. What it can do is to start a question in your brain about what do you value, what can motivate you to take those steps towards healthy behaviors. I don't have to feel bad about not biking a hundred miles a day; I just have to love myself enough to make decisions that will lead to healthier behaviors. This journal is a good step towards my goals.
text_fidelity_b: The Omega Project Black Book Training Journal – US Army Special Operations Elite Workout Planner – Leather Fitness Tracker Notebook Logs Exercise, Sleep, Recovery, Nutrition and More

text_fidelity_a:
Coleman Big Basin Cold-Weather Sleeping Bag, 15°F Big & Tall Camping Sleeping Bag for Adults, Adjustable Hood and Fleece-Lined Footbox for Warmth and Ventilation, Fits Adults up to 6ft 6in Tall I was an Eagle Scout and we've used these bags a few times in temps down to freezing, and they work great if you get a fleece bag liner and put it in there. We were really nice and toasty warm.

PROS:
- HUGE - really really big. I'm 6ft and not small, and there's loads of extra room. If you don't like being cramped, look no further.
- WARM - It's actually pretty darn warm on it's own.
- GOOD ZIPPERS - they're on the left if you're laying in the bag, and they work well without getting caught a lot.
- TWO ZIPPERS - One down the side and one on the bottom. Why is this good? Zippers tend to have issues going around corners, and this seems to help.
- ZIPPER DRAFT TUBE - Huh? They made an extra...insulated tube of fabric next to the zippers running lengthwise that helps keep air out. And it's made of tougher material almost like a backpack which means...drum roll...the zipper finally doesn't get caught on the bag itself!!!
- GOOD HOOD - The hood is really nice and roomy, like put a full size pillow in it roomy. If you sinch it up with the draw string you can have a face-size opening.
- FLEECE FOOT - the inside bottom foot and a half has an extra layer of warm fleece.
- BURROW - I like to kind of burrow down in a sleeping bag and there's so much room you can bend your legs, sleep on your side, have your arm curled under your head, and there's just so much room. I can put my fee at the very bottom and have the opening above my head.
- LOOKS COOL - I know, it's a sleeping bag and how cool do you expect it to look, really? But it really does look pretty cool.

CONS:
- BIG - We put them in stuff sacks that sinch down and they're still pretty big bags.
- NOT FOR BACKPACKING - like everyone says.

HOW TO SLEEP WARMER:
- Put an inexpensive and washable fleece liner inside the bag. There's plenty of room. It adds to the warmth significantly.
- Change your clothes before you sleep. During the day your clothes get moisture from your own body heat. Change before you sleep and not only will you be warmer, having clean clothes inside the bag makes it stay cleaner.
- Don't over-dress. Start off in like shorts and a t-shirt, no socks, and you'll be warm without sweating. If you start off too warm, you'll build up heat, sweat, and then be colder.
- Put your extra layers down in the foot. Got a sweatshirt you'll probably wear in the morning? Shove it down in the foot. There's room, and it'll be warm when you're ready for it in the morning.
- Wear a beanie, helps with heat loss on your head if you stick your head out for fresh air.

FLEECE LINER:
We used something like this (though not this exact one) and it gets even warmer.
https://www.amazon.com/Stansport-Fleece-Sleeping-Bag-Red/dp/B002YXITMW/ref=sr_1_7?dchild=1&keywords=fleece+sleeping+bag+liner&qid=1592870476&sr=8-7

STUFF SACK:
We used a compression stuff sack like this and were able to fit the sleeping bag and the fleece liner in it together.
https://www.amazon.com/Lewis-N-Clark-Compression-Drawstring/dp/B079JRVVD1/ref=sr_1_4?dchild=1&keywords=lewis+n.+clark+compression+sack&qid=1592870350&sr=8-4

This cleaner comes in a large plastic bottle with 32 oz of cleaner in it. The scent is nice- almost like a gentle fruity smell with a twist like bubble gum- but not sickening at all.

She used 3 caps into a bucket of warm water, and she washed as instructed.

FIVE STARS. A little goes a long way and the car looked great when done.

Morpilot 20PSI Paddle Board Pump - Dual Stage Inflation with Powerful SUP Pump Inflator & Deflator, Auto-Off, AC & DC, Intelligent Preset - Perfect for Inflatable Stand-Up Paddle Boards I ordered this item to have a handy way to inflate a slam ball after they lose air over time. Honestly, I wasn't expecting much. However, this little unit worked incredibly well.

It charges quickly via USB Micro (120 minutes to full charge / with 30 inflates per charge), has all of the accessories needed to get going (USB cable, air needles, attachment hose, etc..), has pre-set modes for a football, a soccer ball, a basketball, etc.. And is super compact & lightweight (6.29" x 1.4" & weighing only 6.5oz).

I haven't tried, but don't see why you couldn't even inflate a bicycle tire with this unit as well. However, I probably wouldn't try with anything larger like a car or truck tire out of concern of damaging the pump.

There is an auto-shut off option (IE: when you use a ball preset the pump will turn off when it dispenses the appropriate amount of air for the selected ball), however, there is no pressure gauge. So, if you don't use the preset, then you have to go by feel (or have an air gauge on hand).

As far as my experiment, I didn't even use the presets. Just popped in the needle into my slam ball & turned on the pump. It inflated (my very deflated) slam ball in a matter of seconds. A success!

If you're constantly using a foot pump or bike pump to inflate your sports equipment, bike tires, etc.., then seriously consider this portable pump instead. Makes this process super easy. There's even an attachment that looks like it's to be used for blowing up balloons! Very cool!
text_fidelity_b: Morpilot 20PSI Paddle Board Pump - Dual Stage Inflation with Powerful SUP Pump Inflator & Deflator, Auto-Off, AC & DC, Intelligent Preset - Perfect for Inflatable Stand-Up Paddle Boards

Put one end of the tubing (connected to inlet side) up over the barrel into the water, & pushed the 1/4" outlet tubing (side with arrow pointing out) into the reducer which was screwed onto a 40 ft garden hose which was stretched out uphill.  I wasn't sure this small pump would move water uphill from a 55 gal barrel for that distance, but after several minutes, water started trickling out of the garden hose onto one of the bushes I wanted watered. text_fidelity_a:
NiteRider Omega 300 Taillight On the positive side, this light is extremely bright for a bicycle taillight. The daylight flashing mode (bright light with a random flashing pattern) works great as well. On the negative side, the battery life for this light is disappointing, especially considering the size and weight of the light. I'm getting around 5 hours with the light on the bright mode, which is fine for commuters, but my recreational rides are often more than 5 hours. I could set the light to a dimmer setting that has better battery life, but that defeats the purpose of buying an expensive light. There are many cheaper lights on the market with lower brightness and adequate battery life.

I am also disappointed in the mounts that are included in the package. The seatpost mount can aim the light at different angles (to account for different seatpost angles), but the angle adjustment is less secure than the mounts I have from other brands (which are unfortunately not compatible with this light). The clothing-clip mount is really disappointing because it is not secure. If I clip it on to my belt or to my seat pack, it easily falls off when I run over a pothole. There is no seat stay mount, which does come with some other brands and would work great when I am carrying a seat pack on my seatpost where the seatpost mount would attach.

This light will work great for some people (mostly commuters who ride less than an hour at a time), but there are a lot of other bicycle tail lights on the market that other people should consider.
text_fidelity_b: NiteRider Omega 300 Taillight

am i happy with it? meh. its what i paid for so i cant complain (but i just did complain! lol) - it’ll suit its purpose as a backup reel. its just, i was hoping for the same fit/finish and waulity reel vs some of their other competitors which ive had good luck eith.

CamelBak Magnetic Tube Trap, Grey, One Size I purchased this when I was looking for an alternative to the typical snap and spring clip tube retainer. I like that traditional setup, but I've found the snaps can come loose under strain on occasion, so I thought I'd try something different.

This is pretty good, actually. Mounting the base was tricky - or more, finding a place to mount the base, it isn't quite as versatile as a spring clip, but after I had it in place it kept the tube just where it should be. The magnet is strong enough that it draws the tube in if you get the position relatively right, and it keeps it there pretty much without exception.

It is about even with the spring-clip type in usage. Those kinds of clips have more distance between the clip and the tube, so you have more play and can drink from the tube without needing to unclip it, whereas this one doesn't have that play, but consequently keeps the tube nice and secure instead of flopping about. I'd like to see a slightly wider slot so returning the tube to the base is a bit easier to do without looking, but other than that, would recommend.

After purchasing an Espresso Maker for all of $6 (that is composed of at least ten parts), it was too small to fit on our gas burner. https://smile.amazon.com/gp/product/B00164U4DC/ref=ppx_yo_dt_b_asin_title_o04_s00?ie=UTF8&psc=1

The Ilsa ring is very well made. Any complaints about paint burning off are moot after the first use. Paint is gone, never to smoke again. They really don't need to paint them in the first place. Cast iron skillets aren't painted, and don't need to be.

The ring sits on the stove perfectly.

I can only speak for the black/salmon dual brake pads, but as a Seattle commuter I can say that they are amazing on my hilly, wet commute. The feel of the pads is great--nice gentle engagement without grabbing, and progressive feel throughout the stroke.

This is one of those cheap and easy (seriously, two allen keys and 10 minutes) upgrades that will have you wondering why you waited so long on your stock pads. If you're one of those people who feel the need to spend money on their bike to feel faster, or you can't imagine having an American component on your Italian thoroughbred, go ahead and get the SwissStop brake pads. If you don't, however, have a fetish for ever more expensive bike components go ahead and get the Kool Stop pads and with the money you save get yourself a nice espresso and a croissant on your next few rides.

Calming Cozy by Sharper Image Personal Sherpa Wrap with Electric Heating Massaging Vibrating Foot Bed, 3 Heat & 3 Massage Settings for 9 Relaxing Combinations A few important details about the Calming Cozy by Sharper Image:

✔️ Only the foot portion is heated.
✔️ Even on the highest setting, the heat isn’t very hot.
✔️ The massager is a vibrating massager, very basic.

I expected the whole wrap to be heated, but as I noted, only the foot portion is heated. The blanket part is a normal sherpa blanket. The sherpa is warm and cozy, but I feel like calling it a “heating wrap” is a bit misleading when only the foot area heats up.

The first question in the FAQ is actually “Why doesn’t my Calming Cozy feel hot enough?” So that tells me right there that Sharper Image knows this doesn’t get too warm. The answer in the FAQ is to give the Calming Cozy to heat up -- put it on high and wait 10 minutes. I waited 15 minutes, on high temperature, and still didn’t find it too warm. I tested this out on a 70℉ day and I wasn’t too hot.

I did notice the foot portion holds the heat for a while even after it’s turned off.

The foot massager is vibration only. The light setting is so light as to be ticklish. For the medium and high speeds, my mom heard the vibrations and asked what I was doing. So if you wanted to use this in an office, the massager is not super quiet.

The Calming Cozy has a few nice quality-of-life features. There are two velcro cable ties at the top, to hold the remote so you can easily access it. There is a built-in elastic strap to hold the blanket rolled up when you aren’t using it, for easier, compact storage. There is a zipper on the side, to make it easier to get into and out of the wrap.

The heating element can be removed, so that you can wash the sherpa blanket.

I can see myself using the Calming Cozy at my desk in the winter -- but as a foot and leg blanket only. The heat and vibration just aren’t worth it.
text_fidelity_b: Calming Cozy by Sharper Image Personal Sherpa Wrap with Electric Heating Massaging Vibrating Foot Bed, 3 Heat & 3 Massage Settings for 9 Relaxing Combinations

text_fidelity_a:
Walker's Razor Slim The things I was curious about before buying these:
A) How they sound.
B) How they feel.
C) Compared to Howard Leights by Honeywell as well as the BT edition of the Walker Razor.

I have not tested the Noise Cancellation yet but provided it works as it should I wanted to get out my review in case anyone wondered what I did. My hand's on impressions have been fully positive.
If you get these and wonder how to open the package: I just bent the package in half. This caused the cardboard to split open and the plastic clamshell is not sealed - it is 2 parts and the headphones came out super simple.

How do they sound? (I own Sennheiser HD600 compared to those:)
A)Surprisingly good. Not audiophile but not bad.
B)Bass is light. Not much bass from these. Bass seems purposely reserved, truth be told probably neutral.
C)Slight emphasis on mid-range. But not annoying in any frequency.
D)Highs are present but not pristine.
E)Overall, they sound good for a $43 set of headphones that do so much more. I am pleased with it. I can listen without irritation.

How do they feel?
A) A little tight on my medium-sized head but the muffs are plushy and do a good job of distributing the clamp pressure.
B) I can't imagine wearing these for much more than an hour at a time but it might be ok for longer but probably no one will actually want to.
C) Headband doesn't rub my scalp.
D) No hair pulling or "pinchy parts".
E) The hinges that hold the muffs look thin but they work (so far). Durability could be a concern.
F) The hinges are adjustable. I collapsed then down about 2/5ths of the way so they could possibly fit larger heads but wider heads may have more clamp pressure?
G) Again, the clamp pressure is pretty tight. I am surprised how tight they are. But they stay on the head when moving my head which is good. It is a good thing they are tight but it could cause them to fatigue your head after a while. Be aware they are pretty tight on the head but I don't believe it will be a deal-breaker.

How is the enhanced hearing:
A) Fairly natural. I can rather accurately distinguish sounds.
B) I never knew what a bee flying sounded like other than Bumblebees right in my ear. I heard the bee and I will learn that sound but I wouldn't have known what it was had I not seen the bee and heard the sound.
C) You will discover new sounds you haven't heard before.
D) Unfortunately, the sound is mono-sounding like everyone has said. Determining the origin or placement of noises does not work out so well.
E) I questioned whether to get these or the Howard Leight by Honeywell. I decided to try these first after listening to YouTube videos. I have read reviews that say the "Howard's" better determine which direction noises come from but some videos said they do not do it better enough to choose them over these.
F) These are supposedly more comfortable than the Howard Leights.
G) They are cheaper and look better IMO than the Howard Leights.
H) I might buy the Howard Leights just to see if the sound placement is better because I think that would be a big deal but from what I have read and heard the hype may or may not be all it is cracked up to be. The reviewers mostly chose these over the Howard Leight.

Overall, I am impressed that these are only $43.
Be sure to get a 3.5mm to 3.5mm male to male wire to use them for music.
I wanted to get the Bluetooth version but after reading how much problems people were having with the BT dropping or not working, I decided to get the wired version.
The BT version has 4 mics which, on paper, seems would give better awareness of surroundings but from things I heard it didn't quite work as well in RL as it seems it would. I still would like to try those because it would be worth the money to me if they worked like they should but if they didn't I knew I would still be getting these.
text_fidelity_b: Walker's Razor Slim

text_fidelity_a:
STEARNS Kids Puddle Jumper Deluxe Life Jacket We purchased five different life jackets for the 20 month old twins. The traditionally styled ones rode up at the shoulders. The Swimways Power Swimr System was difficult to get on and did nothing to keep the babies' heads above water. Nor did the Speedo UV 50.

We put the Stearns Kids Puddle Jumper on the first baby and she jumped into the pool for the first time in her life and paddled happily around for hours (see photo). The second twin took a little longer learning how to stay upright and she didn't want to take it off.

On plump babies, it's so tight in the arms that it is hard to get on and off. It's easier if you get both the jacket and their arms slick first (e.g, with sunscreen). However, neither twin complained once they got it on and there were no marks on their arms afterwards.

--------------------
5/12 Update. The twins are now three and can still wear their jackets although they take them off for swimming lessons. Their younger brother is a bit stouter and we have to grease up his chunky arms to get his on him. Another grandbaby on the way so I guess I need to buy a fourth one. The three jackets we have are also used by visiting kids so I realize that they are very tight on really stout kids and really loose on thin kids but, nonetheless, work well on most.

11/12 Update. The end of our third season and the three jackets are good as new. No wearing of the material and little fading despite having been left in the hot Georgia sun much of the time.

3/13 Update. The kids can all swim now but they still ask to have their water wings put on at time because they can just effortlessly float around. And, yes, they have already been swimming this year despite the 65 degree temperature of the pool right now.

7/13 Update. The fourth grandchild refused to wear the wings (or any life jacket). Fine with us since we are always with him and he's learning to swim. Love the new designs for this jacket. I need somebody else's baby to train now.

4/14 Update. Currently selling for $15 at Costco (fewer options)

12/14 Update. We still have the four jackets we purchased. All have faded a little but, otherwise, show no signs of their age.
text_fidelity_b: STEARNS Kids Puddle Jumper Deluxe Life Jacket

text_fidelity_a: NordicTrack T Series Treadmills There is one huge flaw in this machine...and that is if you intend to use the incline feature you will no longer be able to reach anything out in front of you, meaning you can not reach your water bottle...music device...digital read out display...or even to use the heart rate grip handles.  If you look at the machine in the pictures...you will notice a black plastic insert that runs on top of the actual tread mill just below the display.  As you incline the machine...this part of the treadmill comes closer to you....meaning you have to move more backwards on the machine in order to avoid stepping on it.  You have to move back so far that you literally have to bend over at the waist just to use the heart rate grips.  I found myself keep having to step on the sides off the treadmill and stop my walk anytime I wanted to change my music or change a feature on the unit.  Very very frustrating. If you walk for say 30 to 60 minutes and you watch videos on youtube or something like that...you will have to literally stop walking and step off the machine as many times as the videos run out...or your music choice changes.  I don't hold onto the rail in front of me anyway, but if you are someone who does...you will not be able to do so with the unit inclined.  You will keep stepping on the plastic piece and can literally injure yourself the first time you do it.  Machine seems nice otherwise but this is to huge of a flaw to give it anything but 1 star.  I guess everyone else is not using the incline feature.  And no...I am not 8 feet tall....with long legs. Only 5'10" and my wife is 5'1" and has the same issue.  Just note the above and take into consideration when purchasing. I wouldn't buy this unit again...and already put together and box tore up to return.  Frustrating.
text_fidelity_b: NordicTrack T Series Treadmills

text_fidelity_a:
Suunto 3 Fitness Tracker Sports Watch This is a great fitness watch, but it's not that good of a smart watch. I wouldn't suggest cross shopping this with a Samsung Gear or Apple Watch, as they can do quite a bit more than this. Likewise some of the newer Garmin watches are a bit more capable, but if you're looking for a fitness watch (with some smart watch features), this is a very good option.

It sets up quickly, although the charger is more akin to what I expected from 2015 than 2018. It clips on, and it charges reasonably quickly. It has a guided setup and decent instructions that will help walk you through using the watch. I'd rely on those, as it's not the most intuitive watch. Apple and Samsung have them beat there (I haven't used a Garmin). In regards to use, I find the GPS to be quite accurate (compared to phone) and the heart rate and steps to be accurate (compared to a Fitbit). Both do well compared to my own non-scientific tests (ie the heart rate looked right and the recorded journey matched my recollection).

I would say that a Samsung, Apple (if you use iPhones), and Garmin would be more broadly recommended. This is a bit of a fitness watch for fit people (the Garmin fits the bill there), and it's not a "lifestyle accessory" or gizmo. I found the focus on fitness to be refreshing and a bit of a reminder of what I'm trying to do, but I couldn't send tunes to my earbuds or other stuff I can do with some of my other watches. I find it to be a solid tradeoff, but it may not be for you.

4 stars for being a bit niche but not being absolutely amazing at that niche.
text_fidelity_b: Suunto 3 Fitness Tracker Sports Watch

text_fidelity_a:
Fat Gripz Pro - Special Edition Black (New) (2.25" Outer Diameter) --Preamble--

Like many people, I decided to try out some thick bar grips to optimize my current regimen. I too was attracted by the idea of improving my grip and strengthening the whole complex of muscles/tendons/ligaments in my forearms. So I purchased four kinds of wide bar grips - Fat Gripz One (1.75"), Fat Gripz Pro (2.25"), Iron Bull Strength Alpha Grips (2"), and Yes4All Thick Bar Grips (2.2").

Before the review, some context:

First, you should ease into these things, and so if you aren't accustomed to thick bar grips, I would recommend you start with the Fat Gripz One. I did not do this; I tried to integrate all four into my routine, and as a result I gave myself acute tendonitis in both arms, in the form of Golfer's Elbow. Now I need to take at least 4 weeks off while I heal up, and no one likes that. I don't think this would have been a problem if I just started with the narrower grips and moved up from there.

Second, if use a ruler, my hand is 6 5/8" (168mm) from the bend of the wrist to the tip of my middle finger. The Fat Grips One is fine, the Iron Bull Strength grips are about the limit of decent grip, and the Fat Grips Pro are too large to get my hand around, limiting me to fairly light dumbbells. For pull-ups, only the Fat Grips one are comfortable, the Iron Bull's are marginal. I have chronic issues with my TFCC (something I was hoping to help alleviate through these grips) and the thicker ones tend to aggravate that complex.

Lastly, I am fairly fit. I am about 183lbs (83.2kg) and was doing sets of 23 pull-ups before this. I could maintain those numbers with the narrower wide grips, but with greater effort. I have my pull-up bar (an Iron Gym) wrapped in racket grip tape, so it is about 1.1" in diameter. Most of my dumbbells have bars that are between 1.1 and 1.25" in diameter.

--Product Review--

The Fat Gripz Pros are the gold standard for thick bar grips, and for good reason. These do the best at balancing out material, thickness, grippiness, shape, and cost. While these are a bit too thick for my hands, at least at my current stage of development, I think they serve their purposes well.

---Comfort

The Fat Gripz Pros - which are just the same as their standard grips, but in black - are the most comfortable of the grips I tried, tied with the Fat Gripz One. They aren't soft like silicone grips, but they have a little give to them, making it easier to hold them. Their profile makes them easy to hold - i prefer this flat profile to the curved one found in the Iron Bull Alpha grips. The seam has a bit of a hard edge - it could use a chamfer or bevel - but it isn't too distracting. These will not fit IronMaster dumbbells due to those having a 1.25" bar but fit standard CAP weights and my pull-up bar, which have a ~1.1" bar instead.

---Benefit

These are very wide grips, for me anyway, and so they require a significant change in hand position. I had to drop almost 50% of my reps, and 25% of my weight, in order to use them. This means that I just moved these to my lighter dumbbells - currently they are on 25lbs - where I can use them effectively. A bigger guy likely wouldn't have this problem. However, there was a noticeable benefit to how the exercise felt, in my arms, and visually I noticed the forearms were larger and more toned. I think that there would be a lasting benefit to using these if you integrated it into your routine, with mass gains occurring after a month or so. Once I heal up, I intend to continue using them. They don't rotate as much as grips with harder rubber, but you still may need some contact adhesive to keep them in one orientation, especially during pull-ups.

---Conclusion

While I would recommend the Fat Gripz Ones for beginners, and maybe the Iron Bull Alpha Grips 2.0 for people with hands the size of mine, the touted benefits of these appear to be legitimate. I wouldn't expect immediate, wild results, but adding them to the routine is easy and the cumulative benefits will most likely endure. As such, I would recommend them.
text_fidelity_b: Fat Gripz Pro - Special Edition Black (New) (2.25" Outer Diameter)

the best thing about this cooler for longer trips, its dry ice ready. We spent 15$ on dry ice, used the divider (frozen) and our ice didnt start to melt until day 6 on the way home. This cooler worked as well as the Yeti for 3x less money. I'm so happy and proud of my cooler I use it almost everyday. Our beach trip was a total success and we saved 6$ a day on ice at the minimum. Perfect cooler for everyday use, beach, river, lake and just about any time you need. Plenty of room and easy to clean. A must buy

Update, 1st use breakdown.

Did NOT precool cooler, Used Grizzly Brand ice divider (owns Kenia coolers), and my cans were pre chilled in fridge.
I only used 1 half of my cooler using the frozen divider. The other half stayed empty.

10lbs ice 1st day ( rd side ice machine which isnt the best ice and melts quick) after 36 hrs I only had around 2 cups of water because the divider was refreezing the water as it melted against the divider and along the bottom of cooler.
Day 3 I added 20lbs of frozen ice. Still only half of cooler. Didnt have but a quart or so of melt off by this point and divider was half melted. The ice last 2 more days before I drained 1.25 to 1.5 gallons of water from cooler and had maybe 7 lbs of lightly frozen ice left.

This cooler is awesome from my use and my experience with using it. Today I've added 20lbs of ice NO divider and using entire cooler and I still only have a cup of water. Temp is 80 degrees constantly and 15 hrs have gone by already. This is still the rd side machine ice, as I said before in a normal cooler 20lbs will melt within 20 hrs for sure by next morning it's all water. With the Kenia cooler I have easily doubled my ice time if not almost tripling it. And I'm not freezing the ice in a freezer before use. If you freeze this crap ice before use, it can last 4 or so days. If u freeze ice in deep freezer I'm sure it will last even longer because of the - temps with deep freezer.

Well worth the money spent and saved vs a 600$ equivalent yeti. This cooler will pay for it self over 40 total days, 5$ or more per bag ice, 1 bag per day 200$... paid for that quick. At least with my old coolers this is what I was having to do, either 6$ bag ice from store or 2 rd side bags @4$ per day. Every day and during our Southern 100 degree days I was having to do this twice a day. So by far this cooler out last most on market.

Now I added 20 lbs of frozen freezer ice to that 10lbs, didnt drain the water. The ice lasted 4 days. I hope this helps someone make the right choice for the money.
We have a beach trip planned in few months and another updated test results will come after that trip. That test will be outside in middle summer outside 16+ hrs a day in direct sunlight. Will update after words to tell the world.

text_fidelity_a:
Mother Earth Products Zucchini, Quart Jar, 8 oz Pointing out a few things brought up in reviews:

1. This is DEHYDRATED zucchini, NOT freeze-dried. Very different methods, different results, different pricing. While Mother Earth does carry some freeze dried, they do not have freeze dried zucchini. Another way to tell? With freeze dried foods, they can be eaten as is (crunchy snack) or rehydrated. Where as with dehydrated foods, most all (except fruits, usually) will need to be rehydrated in order to consume them (too tough to eat). This will require soaking and/or cooking for a period of time. Can't just toss it in the dish you are making and expect it to cook up quickly. So for this, it says to simmer 1 part zucchini to 2 parts water for 10-30 minutes. This very well may take longer. I let it cook for no less than 30 minutes before adding it to what I ultimately want to have it be part of. Another way to get it started is to let soak, then follow up with a shorter simmer.

2. 1/2 cup dried zucchini = 1 cup cooked zucchini. I made up 1/4 cup and it made a very good sized portion. See my pics.

3. End result is NOT EVER going to be same as fresh. Stop that. Then stop blaming the company/brand. YOu will always be disappointed. Best thing to get if you cant get fresh or frozen is to find a company who makes freeze dried. Even then, you are expecting a lot from zucchini. This is similar to others, and there aren't many out there to choose from.

4. Shelf life can be very very long, if not indefinite if stored under proper conditions. Freeze dried for sure, but dehydrated can last a very long time. Be sure to keep it in well sealed container, out of light and dampness. Maybe keep in freezer or further repackaged into mylar or vac sealed jar.

5. Taste is neutral. Kind of like how zucchini can be. I could tell it was zucchini though! I found that with proper rehydration it worked well in adding bulk to tacos, and can always be added to soup. I see it as a nutritional item rather than a way to have a plate of zucchini. Nice way to bulk up meals, add vitamins and minerals, yet not have to rely on fresh (for various reasons). I noticed that the skins were more like late summer yellow squash/zucchini. Kinda reminded me of regular squash- like butternut skins. Not tough but had more "presence" I shall say. DID not taste or feel like "tree bark" in any way.

6. If planning on using it in zucchini bread, muffins, cookies, or sauces, I would recommend running it through the blender after it has been rehydrated. Make it more of a puree. This will impart flavor and decrease any tougher bits.

7. Says processed and packaged in USA, but WHERE do they get their vegetables from?? That I havent seen, here or on their web page

8. If you dont like this packaging, they also offer mylar bag style.

OVERALL: I think it is fine, and it as expected. I love seeing it in my pantry knowing that I have a variety of dehydrated foods to use when I cant get fresh, or food is scarce, or food doesnt look good, or I cant afford it that day. Buy a little here and there and stock up those cupboards. Would like to know where the zucchini comes from?

PS. I miss when we could comment and ask questions of other reviewers. One person just said "poisonous". Like, what do they even mean by that? I had this a few times and doing well so far :)
text_fidelity_b: Mother Earth Products Zucchini, Quart Jar, 8 oz

Schwinn Wayfarer Adult Bike Hybrid Retro-Styled Cruiser, Step-Over or Step-Through Frame Option, 7-Speed Drivetrain, Rear Rack, 700C Wheels, Multiple Colors This is a very good bike for the price. Some people are like 'oh it took only a few hours to put together', but I am a student who has a flexible schedule and I can say it took longer than a few hours. The initial assembly took a few hours - around 4 - but the tweaking took a few days. When I first put it together I felt glorious - like I had finished building a colosseum. I decide to take this work of art out for a spin at 11pm. Once I get outside, I get onto the sidewalk and prepare for take off. I mount the bike and immediately take a dive as both the seat and handle bar give in. It was painful.. for my ego. So I go back inside and tinker away. Then come out and hooray, the seat is kind of stable, but the handlebar is shaky. I throw caution to the wind and start riding.. or peddling.. then I see that the chain is like not in place or something? I'm not a mechanic. But I use some of the wisdom my father passed on to me to fix the chain (align it with the gear.. it was not hard or complicated lol.. but if you're not expecting it, then you feel like a fool).. anyway, I am telling you all of this so that when you buy this awesome bike, you won't feel disheartened by the fact that it might not take a minute to put together. Also, don't go to a repair person until you just need it to be tightened.. because you'll have a much better experience if you know why your bike messes up and how to fix it easily when it does. I ended up going to get it tightened because the seat and handlebar war just not tightening with my arm. So the guy who did it also gave my bike a check up and totally validated my pride by saying I did a great job. He only charged $5 for labor (but others did the same for free). Another bike repair man filled my bike with air and also adjusted the seat for me, since I had it a bit high. A lot of people will give you advice on how to sit on your bike, but don't change all the time. Test it out, and if it feels weird and to laborious then go back. Sometimes the advice is for efficiency, but a lot of times it given by veteran bikers who found their way after years of biking.
anyway, good luck.

text_fidelity_a: SABRE Runner Pepper Gel, Maximum Police Strength OC Spray, Reflective Hand Strap for Easy Carry & Quick Access, 35 Bursts, Secure & Easy to Use Safety, Optional Clip-On Alarm & LED Armband Combos The Sabre Red Runner Pepper Gel personal alarm is a product you don’t want to review after having to use it.  But looking it over thoroughly I find it to be very well thought out.  It’s about the size of a tube of mascara yet weighs less.  Hardly noticeable when strapped to my arm.  The comfortable adjustable strap and uncomplicated trigger safety – just slide the red trigger over about half an inch then push to spray – make it appear to be simple to use, even in a frightened state.  But what I like best is the alarm that comes with it.  It has a very sturdy clip that can be successfully attached to a flimsy T-shirt or a fairly thick coat.  There is a green light that has three options: On, Slow flash, and Fast flash.  The light is also used to test the battery.  Holding the light button down for 3 seconds and seeing if the light quickly flashes green or red indicates battery strength.  The four LR44 batteries (included) can be replaced.  I think the alarm alone would deter most criminals.  To say it’s loud is an understatement.  The brochure states to avoid prolonged exposure as it could cause permanent hearing loss.  I’d recommend trying this away from children and pets.  It is painfully loud!  I hope I never need it but I’m glad I have it.

text_fidelity_a:
Fitbit Charge HR Wireless Activity Wristband (Tangerine, Large (6.2 - 7.6 in)) UPDATE 10/10/2018:
Now the device is useless - the charging cable will not stay in the tracker, so it cannot be charged. The piece that is depressed to see the display has disappeared (photo). No idea where it is. That is one-half of the poor design. The proprietary charging connector is the other half.
The strap had a piece that kept the loose end from doing whatever it wanted. That also broke. It was replaced with an O-ring that seemed to work for several months.

UPDATE 7/17/2016: The Charge HR has lost its sync - in less than 24 hours! One more star removed. It should maintain the synchronization for longer than that. The company has known of this problem since AT LEAST this past March.

Bought this for my wife - direct from fitbit. Price has dropped since then.

According to the fitbit company / site, it needs to be synced - loses that connection after a few minutes to a few days. One star removed. fitbit needs to get its software updated to maintain the connection. It worked fine the first year before the recent update.

The plastic piece that is the contact button for viewing the various parts of the display came off when my wife removed the Charge HR from her wrist to charge it. I used a drop of instant glue on the side away from the button. It came off again a couple of weeks later. A small drop of glue was placed on both sides of the plastic piece so it cannot come loose from the Charge HR. A second star was removed.

text_fidelity_a:
SOG Specialty Knives SAT002-BX Flashback Tini Knife, Black SOG has been in the industry a long time. They offer an affordable value in the knife world. They constantly try to innovate and carry Lifetime Warranties on their products. Some of their designs are fantastic. Some are duds. The Flashback is an awesome every day carry folder that is nearly perfect but just misses shy. I still managed to pick up this straight clip model as well as a tanto version.

Packaging: This is the black box version. Not the retail box version. It doesn't matter, you get the same knife in both boxes but one doesn't have a clear window to view the blade and the other is just a black manufacturer's box that says SOG. It's not about the box, it's about what's inside.

First glance: This thing screams cool. I just love the color scheme, look of the blade, the total design reminds me of a slick silver on black race car set up. The clip is reversible, but already comes in my preferred carry designation. It rides deep in the pocket and retains firmly to the pocket. I haven't had one instance of it coming loose or getting hung up on seatbelts or the like in my daily use.

Picking it up: I believe SOG advertises these Flashback knives around 3.8 oz. It feels heavier, but I don't have a scale to confirm. Either way, it's fairly light. Disable the safety, and then never use it again. I'm actually of the mindset SOG should just delete their safeties on most of their assisted folders, but your mileage may vary. If it gives you a warm fuzzy to use it, then do so. I think it just takes away from the attractiveness of the design and is unnecessary. First use flicking it open and you realize SOG really meant this thing was fast. It opens authoritatively, too, so hold on to it. Snaps into a firm lock position and is ready to use. The blade is AUS-8 steel and comes hair shaving sharp out of the box. AUS-8 is OK, but I wish SOG would use some better steels in their builds. It'll be fine for the use of everyday carry, however. I'm not a huge Tanto fan, but I had to have that model in addition to this straight clip Flashback I picked up due to how much I liked the straight clip after carrying a few days. The Tanto was supposed to be a gift, but I think I'm keeping it, too. As for the grip, you can get a firm purchase on the blade as a result of the aggressive gimping. I think SOG nailed this one unlike some of their other designs. It fits my hand so well and provides a level of confidence in use as result.

Build Quality: Now here's where things get tricky. SOG is a mass market knife maker. Meaning they pump them out, check on the quality so often, and use cheap labor to build it. One example can be outstanding in build and the next will be ok for the value. The tanto I received has perfect blade centering. The straight clip model is off to one side. Both are well built, but inherent in a lot of SOG designs there is some side-to-side play in each once the blade is in the locked position. It has something to do with their locking design as it was also inherent in the Aegis I've previously owned. This is where I knock these knives down a star as others in the same price category like Cold Steel and Spyderco don't have these issues.

Overall: I love carrying this knife. I do prefer the straight clip blade design and would recommend that to purchasers as the blade shape is more useful, at least to me. I still had to have this tanto version in addition. There are some caveats that come in the mass-produced build quality, but if you want a well-built everyday folder that has a solid value than you shouldn't be disappointed in the Flashbacks from SOG. I would suggest shopping around a bit and making sure you do get the best price, however, as these can fluctuate. With a few shortcomings, this still comes as a recommended buy.
text_fidelity_b: SOG Specialty Knives SAT002-BX Flashback Tini Knife, Black
